bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Globalbees' last brand acquisition was in September 2022; growth since then is described as organic, alongside completed rationalization of other brands — i.e. consolidation rather than further M&A.
- Fully diluted share capitalisation of 532.4 Mn as of June 30, 2026 versus 522.1 Mn basic shares (98.1%), with 0.5 Mn time-based ESOPs (0.1%) and 9.8 Mn performance-based ESOPs (1.8%) whose vesting is linked to market capitalization.

- The deck defines Free Cash Flow as net cash generated in operating activities less acquisition of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and leasehold land.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Home brands as a differentiated, exclusive assortment: during FY 2025-26 home brands contributed over 58% of India Multi-Channel Business GMV, deepening loyalty and improving structural margins with products available nowhere else.
- BabyHug is India's largest multi-category MBK products brand by GMV and carries one of the largest product assortments in the Asia-Pacific region excluding China.
- A hospital-led customer acquisition engine no competitor has: long-standing partnerships with 13,500+ hospitals and maternity clinics across India, through which over 2.4 Million FirstCry-branded baby boxes were distributed during FY 2025-26.
- Full-stack operating model with end-to-end control across sourcing, manufacturing and fulfilment, resting on 800+ contract manufacturing partners across India and overseas plus in-house diaper manufacturing through Swara Baby, Swara Hygiene and Solis Hygiene.
- Proprietary last-mile logistics: RocketBees expanded from 4 to 62 cities during FY 2025-26, delivering approximately 20% faster turnaround times than third-party logistics providers while handling over 40% of online shipment volumes, with FirstCry Qwik delivering in under three hours by turning stores into local fulfilment hubs.
- Omnichannel cross-pollination as a durable moat: 36% of India GMV across the top 50 cities came from customers shopping across both online and offline channels, and such customers show structurally higher basket values, purchase frequency and loyalty.
- A warehouse and delivery network supporting same-day delivery across 25+ cities and next-day delivery across 980+ cities, backed by 84 warehouses and stockists as at March 31, 2026.
- Long customer lifecycle in the parenting category: as children's needs evolve from infancy to adolescence, families keep buying across categories, holding retention high and lifting transaction value year after year.
- A content, community and technology layer that extends the relationship past the point of sale: one of India's largest in-house influencer programmes in the MBK category, a large engaged parenting community, AI tools including Parenting GPT, and 193 Million FirstCry app downloads.
- Category resilience: approximately 85% of GMV comes from non-diapering products, insulating the business from the diapering discounting cycle, and childcare spending is predominantly non-discretionary.
- Market leadership in the GCC: FirstCry is the largest specialist online retailer for MBK products in the UAE by GMV and the leading online-first specialist platform in KSA.
- A proprietary Product Lifecycle Management platform supporting faster innovation, stronger quality assurance and efficient management of home brands.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive landscape risk from horizontal e-commerce, quick-commerce players and offline retailers — Intensifying competition from horizontal e-commerce platforms, quick-commerce players, offline retailers and new entrants in the baby, kids and mother-care segments may erode differentiation and private-label strength, causing customer churn, reduced pricing power, higher customer acquisition and retention costs, and pressure on gross margins and market share. The diapering sub-category in particular saw large horizontal platforms run sustained promotional discounting during FY 2025-26 that pressured growth and margins.
- Product quality and safety risk across a third-party manufacturing base — Inadequate quality controls or non-compliance with BIS standards and certification requirements may allow defective or unsafe products to reach customers. Risk is amplified by reliance on 800+ contract manufacturing partners: third-party manufacturing deficiencies, testing or dispatch control gaps, traceability gaps or changes in applicable standards could trigger complaints, recalls, regulatory penalties, loss or suspension of certifications and reputational damage in a category where parental trust is the core asset.
- Cyber security and customer data protection risk — The Company collects customer data across online and offline channels, so phishing, malware, insider action, third-party vulnerabilities, misconfiguration or inadequate monitoring could cause unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, loss or destruction of sensitive data. Such incidents would bring operational disruption, financial loss, regulatory and compliance exposure and reputational damage that would undermine the credibility of a platform business built on parental trust.
- Supply chain and logistics dependency risk — Vulnerabilities across the end-to-end logistics network, including last-mile e-commerce delivery, warehouse operations, replenishment of offline stores and clearance of imported merchandise, may cause delivery failures, transit damage, fulfilment delays and stock-outs. Cost escalation, operational dependencies and inadequate contractual safeguards further raise disruption risk, hitting supply chain efficiency, customer experience, revenue and brand reputation.
- Vendor ecosystem and macroeconomic factor risk, including vendor concentration and import dependence — Volatility in raw material prices, foreign exchange rates, freight costs, geopolitical conditions and broader macroeconomic factors, combined with vendor concentration and supplier dependency, may raise landed costs and disrupt supply timelines. This bites hardest in import-dependent categories and third-party consumables. Competitive intensity and price sensitivity may prevent passing on increased costs, compressing gross margins and profitability.
- Attrition, talent retention and succession planning risk — High employee attrition, limited talent retention, inadequate succession planning and over-dependence on key personnel may cause operational disruption, productivity loss, inconsistent service quality and leadership gaps. Loss of critical knowledge and higher hiring and training costs would further hit business continuity. The need for regular hiring across stores nationwide plus continuous training and upskilling makes human capital management a standing challenge.
- Legal, regulatory and compliance risk, including tax and customs proceedings — Non-compliance with applicable laws, contractual obligations and evolving regulatory requirements, including ESG, data protection, labour and statutory reporting obligations, may result from inadequate monitoring, delayed or inaccurate filings, or gaps in compliance controls, exposing the Company to penalties, civil or criminal liability, higher compliance costs and reputational damage. The BRSR discloses multiple live monetary proceedings under appeal, spanning Legal Metrology compounding fees, a customs differential duty and penalty order, a GST demand order and an income-tax transfer pricing and ESOP disallowance assessment.
- Marketplace and channel policy dependency risk — Evolving marketplace policies during the year, most notably Flipkart's revised revenue recognition and settlement framework, reinforced the importance of holding diversified customer acquisition channels. Brands with concentrated marketplace exposure proved less resilient to these platform-level disruptions, making dependence on external platforms a structural exposure for the GlobalBees D2C portfolio in particular.

outlook.body:
- Build one integrated parenting platform rather than a set of separate businesses, so that stores, digital commerce, home brands, the education business and the fulfilment network reinforce one another and each new connection makes the whole worth more.
- Shift the operating focus from widening the footprint to getting more from existing assets: deepening inventory across high-demand categories, sharpening procurement efficiency and lifting store productivity within the India Multi-Channel Business.
- Judge every major investment, whether in technology, home brands, fulfilment infrastructure or customer engagement, on its ability to create stronger unit economics, improve capital efficiency and deliver sustainable shareholder value, rather than investing solely to expand scale.
- Expand home brands to improve product mix, widen gross margins and increase customer loyalty, with home brands positioned as growth engines offering differentiated products across categories, age groups and price points.
- Build proprietary last-mile and quick-commerce capability through RocketBees and FirstCry Qwik to gain control over fulfilment, reduce reliance on third-party logistics partners and create operating leverage, accepting near-term cost pressure for long-term efficiency.
- Diversify customer acquisition channels and strengthen direct engagement through the FirstCry app, the omnichannel network and proprietary fulfilment, reducing dependence on external marketplace platforms after evolving marketplace policies during the year.
- In the International Business, pursue quality-first customer acquisition prioritising retention and lifetime value over discount-led growth, raise home-brand penetration particularly in fashion and private labels, expand omnichannel presence, and localise the customer experience through bilingual English and Arabic platforms and region-specific merchandising.
- At GlobalBees, having completed the acquisition phase, prioritise quality of growth over portfolio expansion through portfolio rationalisation and operational discipline, accepting held-back reported revenues to strengthen the long-term earnings profile.
- Widen the use of AI and generative AI across customer engagement, merchandising and internal operations, and expand engineering, product and data science teams to support AI-enabled personalisation and intelligent recommendations.
- Use the Education Business to engage families at the earliest stage of a child's life, feeding the wider platform strategy while generating healthy returns in its own right.
- Sharpen merchandise assortment around the emerging needs and preferences of Millennial and Gen Z parents, and make demand-generation and engagement efforts more relevant to how today's young families discover, evaluate and choose products.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FirstCry is an asset-light multi-channel retail platform, and its expansion during FY 2025-26 was in footprint, fulfilment infrastructure and platform build-out rather than in manufacturing capacity. The BRSR Section A operations table reports zero plants and 266 national locations, comprising 3 offices, 10 warehouses, 250 stores and 3 hubs for the listed entity on a standalone basis, with no international locations; markets served span 22 states where the Company holds GST registrations plus 2 countries. At group level the modern retail network grew to 1,189 stores and the Corporate Overview reports 84 warehouses and stockists as at March 31, 2026. The most significant expansion of the year was RocketBees, the proprietary in-house logistics network, which expanded from 4 to 62 cities, delivering approximately 20% faster turnaround times than third-party logistics providers while handling over 40% of online shipment volumes; alongside it FirstCry Qwik was rolled out, delivering the specialist assortment in under three hours by turning stores into local fulfilment hubs. The warehouse network supports same-day delivery across 25+ cities and next-day delivery across 980+ cities. Management explicitly describes a shift in operational priority away from widening the footprint towards getting more from existing assets, deepening inventory across high-demand categories and lifting store productivity, and notes these fulfilment investments created near-term cost pressures in exchange for control over last-mile delivery. Manufacturing sits in subsidiaries rather than the listed entity: diapering capability is held through Swara Baby Products, Swara Hygiene and Solis Hygiene, and home-brand production rests on 800+ contract manufacturing partners across India and overseas. Swara Baby added capability inorganically during the year, acquiring 100% of K.A. Enterprises (Hygiene) on December 25, 2025 and 100% of Solis Hygiene on December 30, 2025, and incorporating Swara Corp. in Delaware, USA on December 08, 2025. Internationally, the Company opened its first FirstCry-branded store in Riyadh during FY 2025-26, extending omnichannel expansion into KSA alongside the existing UAE business. The Education Business network expanded to 436 preschools across 190+ cities, serving 23,049 students enrolled during FY 2025-26. Energy-related site investments include a rooftop solar panel system commissioned at the Pune warehouse, smart sensors and rooftop skylights across the warehouse network, roof insulation, louvers, ridge ventilation and HVLS BLDC fans, and battery-powered material handling equipment at warehouses. GlobalBees has completed its acquisition phase and is now prioritising quality of growth over portfolio expansion, so no further inorganic brand additions are indicated there.

outlook.body:
- Childcare spending is predominantly non-discretionary, making the category structurally resilient across economic cycles; rising parental awareness of product quality, safety and authenticity continues to deepen the shift towards trusted, branded childcare products and platforms.
- The GST rationalisation of FY 2025-26, which brought a broad range of childcare and consumer products into the lower 5% tax bracket, is expected to function as a multi-year structural tailwind, improving affordability, accelerating formalisation and widening the competitive advantage of branded organised players over unorganised alternatives.
- Tier II and Tier III cities emerged as the fastest-growing markets for organised childcare retail, e-commerce and branded consumer products, and accounted for over 60% of e-commerce transactions in India in FY 2025-26, expanding the addressable market well beyond the top metros.
- Rising disposable incomes and parental spending intent: emerging and mature income households are expected to represent 74% of all Indian households by FY 2028-29, and health, hygiene and developmental spending for children is increasingly treated as a non-negotiable priority.
- Nuclearisation of families and dual-income households drives demand for convenience-oriented, quality-assured childcare products, while shorter replacement cycles across the 0-12 year age spectrum create a structurally recurring demand base.
- Premiumisation: India's Millennial and Gen Z parenting cohort shows a pronounced preference for premium, safe and quality-assured products with transparent ingredient sourcing and safety certifications, driving trading-up across baby skincare, apparel and developmental toys.
- Quick commerce has structurally elevated consumer expectations on delivery speed and reliability across all retail formats, giving retailers who invested ahead of the curve in proprietary delivery infrastructure a meaningful competitive advantage over third-party logistics networks.
- The omnichannel cross-pollination effect continues to deepen: customers transacting across both physical and digital touchpoints show structurally higher basket values, greater purchase frequency and stronger brand loyalty, emerging as one of the most durable competitive moats for specialist multi-channel retailers.
- Non-apparel categories including consumables, hard goods and toys grew faster than apparel during FY 2025-26, reflecting higher per-transaction basket values and greater parental willingness to invest in developmental and lifestyle products.
- The diapering sub-category faced a distinct near-term headwind as large horizontal e-commerce platforms ran elevated promotional and discounting activity; management expects competitive dynamics to normalise as the market matures and players reassess unit economics, with underlying non-discretionary demand intact.
- The GCC opportunity rests on significantly higher spending per child than India, young populations, favourable birth rates, expanding female workforce participation and continued digital commerce growth, particularly in Saudi Arabia under Vision 2030.
- In India's D2C market, marketplace policy changes during the year, most notably Flipkart's revised revenue recognition and settlement framework, prompted brands to accelerate multi-platform distribution; organic acquisition-driven growth without inorganic portfolio additions became the marker of genuinely strong D2C businesses.
- The Indian macro backdrop remains supportive heading into FY 2026-27, with the IMF projecting GDP growth of 6.4%, the World Bank 6.5% and the Economic Survey a range of 6.8-7.2%, and inflation projected to converge toward the RBI's 4% target.

deepdive.thesis: Brainbees achieved consolidated free cash flow positivity in FY26 despite 140bps gross margin compression from diaper price wars and input cost inflation, betting on insourced logistics (RocketBees/Qwik) and offline store depth to drive superior FY27 growth. While near-term EBITDA faces headwinds from front-loaded logistics costs and irrational discounting, the structural shift to 40%+ self-delivered orders and 15% offline GMV growth signals a turnaround in customer experience and unit economics ahead.

risks.note: Intensifying competition from horizontal e-commerce platforms, quick-commerce players, offline retailers and new entrants in the baby, kids and mother-care segments may erode differentiation and private-label strength, causing customer churn, reduced pricing power, higher customer acquisition and retention costs, and pressure on gross margins and market share. The diapering sub-category in particular saw large horizontal platforms run sustained promotional discounting during FY 2025-26 that pressured growth and margins.
risks.risk: Competitive landscape risk from horizontal e-commerce, quick-commerce players and offline retailers

risks.note: Inadequate quality controls or non-compliance with BIS standards and certification requirements may allow defective or unsafe products to reach customers. Risk is amplified by reliance on 800+ contract manufacturing partners: third-party manufacturing deficiencies, testing or dispatch control gaps, traceability gaps or changes in applicable standards could trigger complaints, recalls, regulatory penalties, loss or suspension of certifications and reputational damage in a category where parental trust is the core asset.
risks.risk: Product quality and safety risk across a third-party manufacturing base

risks.note: The Company collects customer data across online and offline channels, so phishing, malware, insider action, third-party vulnerabilities, misconfiguration or inadequate monitoring could cause unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, loss or destruction of sensitive data. Such incidents would bring operational disruption, financial loss, regulatory and compliance exposure and reputational damage that would undermine the credibility of a platform business built on parental trust.
risks.risk: Cyber security and customer data protection risk

risks.note: Vulnerabilities across the end-to-end logistics network, including last-mile e-commerce delivery, warehouse operations, replenishment of offline stores and clearance of imported merchandise, may cause delivery failures, transit damage, fulfilment delays and stock-outs. Cost escalation, operational dependencies and inadequate contractual safeguards further raise disruption risk, hitting supply chain efficiency, customer experience, revenue and brand reputation.
risks.risk: Supply chain and logistics dependency risk

risks.note: Volatility in raw material prices, foreign exchange rates, freight costs, geopolitical conditions and broader macroeconomic factors, combined with vendor concentration and supplier dependency, may raise landed costs and disrupt supply timelines. This bites hardest in import-dependent categories and third-party consumables. Competitive intensity and price sensitivity may prevent passing on increased costs, compressing gross margins and profitability.
risks.risk: Vendor ecosystem and macroeconomic factor risk, including vendor concentration and import dependence

risks.note: High employee attrition, limited talent retention, inadequate succession planning and over-dependence on key personnel may cause operational disruption, productivity loss, inconsistent service quality and leadership gaps. Loss of critical knowledge and higher hiring and training costs would further hit business continuity. The need for regular hiring across stores nationwide plus continuous training and upskilling makes human capital management a standing challenge.
risks.risk: Attrition, talent retention and succession planning risk

risks.note: Non-compliance with applicable laws, contractual obligations and evolving regulatory requirements, including ESG, data protection, labour and statutory reporting obligations, may result from inadequate monitoring, delayed or inaccurate filings, or gaps in compliance controls, exposing the Company to penalties, civil or criminal liability, higher compliance costs and reputational damage. The BRSR discloses multiple live monetary proceedings under appeal, spanning Legal Metrology compounding fees, a customs differential duty and penalty order, a GST demand order and an income-tax transfer pricing and ESOP disallowance assessment.
risks.risk: Legal, regulatory and compliance risk, including tax and customs proceedings

risks.note: Evolving marketplace policies during the year, most notably Flipkart's revised revenue recognition and settlement framework, reinforced the importance of holding diversified customer acquisition channels. Brands with concentrated marketplace exposure proved less resilient to these platform-level disruptions, making dependence on external platforms a structural exposure for the GlobalBees D2C portfolio in particular.
risks.risk: Marketplace and channel policy dependency risk

risks.risk: Competitive landscape risk from horizontal e-commerce, quick-commerce players and offline retailers
risks.note: Intensifying competition from horizontal e-commerce platforms, quick-commerce players, offline retailers and new entrants in the baby, kids and mother-care segments may erode differentiation and private-label strength, causing customer churn, reduced pricing power, higher customer acquisition and retention costs, and pressure on gross margins and market share. The diapering sub-category in particular saw large horizontal platforms run sustained promotional discounting during FY 2025-26 that pressured growth and margins.

risks.risk: Product quality and safety risk across a third-party manufacturing base
risks.note: Inadequate quality controls or non-compliance with BIS standards and certification requirements may allow defective or unsafe products to reach customers. Risk is amplified by reliance on 800+ contract manufacturing partners: third-party manufacturing deficiencies, testing or dispatch control gaps, traceability gaps or changes in applicable standards could trigger complaints, recalls, regulatory penalties, loss or suspension of certifications and reputational damage in a category where parental trust is the core asset.

risks.risk: Cyber security and customer data protection risk
risks.note: The Company collects customer data across online and offline channels, so phishing, malware, insider action, third-party vulnerabilities, misconfiguration or inadequate monitoring could cause unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, loss or destruction of sensitive data. Such incidents would bring operational disruption, financial loss, regulatory and compliance exposure and reputational damage that would undermine the credibility of a platform business built on parental trust.

risks.risk: Supply chain and logistics dependency risk
risks.note: Vulnerabilities across the end-to-end logistics network, including last-mile e-commerce delivery, warehouse operations, replenishment of offline stores and clearance of imported merchandise, may cause delivery failures, transit damage, fulfilment delays and stock-outs. Cost escalation, operational dependencies and inadequate contractual safeguards further raise disruption risk, hitting supply chain efficiency, customer experience, revenue and brand reputation.

risks.risk: Vendor ecosystem and macroeconomic factor risk, including vendor concentration and import dependence
risks.note: Volatility in raw material prices, foreign exchange rates, freight costs, geopolitical conditions and broader macroeconomic factors, combined with vendor concentration and supplier dependency, may raise landed costs and disrupt supply timelines. This bites hardest in import-dependent categories and third-party consumables. Competitive intensity and price sensitivity may prevent passing on increased costs, compressing gross margins and profitability.

risks.risk: Attrition, talent retention and succession planning risk
risks.note: High employee attrition, limited talent retention, inadequate succession planning and over-dependence on key personnel may cause operational disruption, productivity loss, inconsistent service quality and leadership gaps. Loss of critical knowledge and higher hiring and training costs would further hit business continuity. The need for regular hiring across stores nationwide plus continuous training and upskilling makes human capital management a standing challenge.

risks.risk: Legal, regulatory and compliance risk, including tax and customs proceedings
risks.note: Non-compliance with applicable laws, contractual obligations and evolving regulatory requirements, including ESG, data protection, labour and statutory reporting obligations, may result from inadequate monitoring, delayed or inaccurate filings, or gaps in compliance controls, exposing the Company to penalties, civil or criminal liability, higher compliance costs and reputational damage. The BRSR discloses multiple live monetary proceedings under appeal, spanning Legal Metrology compounding fees, a customs differential duty and penalty order, a GST demand order and an income-tax transfer pricing and ESOP disallowance assessment.

risks.risk: Marketplace and channel policy dependency risk
risks.note: Evolving marketplace policies during the year, most notably Flipkart's revised revenue recognition and settlement framework, reinforced the importance of holding diversified customer acquisition channels. Brands with concentrated marketplace exposure proved less resilient to these platform-level disruptions, making dependence on external platforms a structural exposure for the GlobalBees D2C portfolio in particular.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Childcare spending is predominantly non-discretionary, making the category structurally resilient across economic cycles; rising parental awareness of product quality, safety and authenticity continues to deepen the shift towards trusted, branded childcare products and platforms.
- The GST rationalisation of FY 2025-26, which brought a broad range of childcare and consumer products into the lower 5% tax bracket, is expected to function as a multi-year structural tailwind, improving affordability, accelerating formalisation and widening the competitive advantage of branded organised players over unorganised alternatives.

- Rising disposable incomes and parental spending intent: emerging and mature income households are expected to represent 74% of all Indian households by FY 2028-29, and health, hygiene and developmental spending for children is increasingly treated as a non-negotiable priority.
- Nuclearisation of families and dual-income households drives demand for convenience-oriented, quality-assured childcare products, while shorter replacement cycles across the 0-12 year age spectrum create a structurally recurring demand base.
- Premiumisation: India's Millennial and Gen Z parenting cohort shows a pronounced preference for premium, safe and quality-assured products with transparent ingredient sourcing and safety certifications, driving trading-up across baby skincare, apparel and developmental toys.
- Quick commerce has structurally elevated consumer expectations on delivery speed and reliability across all retail formats, giving retailers who invested ahead of the curve in proprietary delivery infrastructure a meaningful competitive advantage over third-party logistics networks.
- The omnichannel cross-pollination effect continues to deepen: customers transacting across both physical and digital touchpoints show structurally higher basket values, greater purchase frequency and stronger brand loyalty, emerging as one of the most durable competitive moats for specialist multi-channel retailers.
- Non-apparel categories including consumables, hard goods and toys grew faster than apparel during FY 2025-26, reflecting higher per-transaction basket values and greater parental willingness to invest in developmental and lifestyle products.
- The diapering sub-category faced a distinct near-term headwind as large horizontal e-commerce platforms ran elevated promotional and discounting activity; management expects competitive dynamics to normalise as the market matures and players reassess unit economics, with underlying non-discretionary demand intact.
- The GCC opportunity rests on significantly higher spending per child than India, young populations, favourable birth rates, expanding female workforce participation and continued digital commerce growth, particularly in Saudi Arabia under Vision 2030.
- In India's D2C market, marketplace policy changes during the year, most notably Flipkart's revised revenue recognition and settlement framework, prompted brands to accelerate multi-platform distribution; organic acquisition-driven growth without inorganic portfolio additions became the marker of genuinely strong D2C businesses.
- The Indian macro backdrop remains supportive heading into FY 2026-27, with the IMF projecting GDP growth of 6.4%, the World Bank 6.5% and the Economic Survey a range of 6.8-7.2%, and inflation projected to converge toward the RBI's 4% target.

moat.body:
- Home brands as a differentiated, exclusive assortment: during FY 2025-26 home brands contributed over 58% of India Multi-Channel Business GMV, deepening loyalty and improving structural margins with products available nowhere else.
- BabyHug is India's largest multi-category MBK products brand by GMV and carries one of the largest product assortments in the Asia-Pacific region excluding China.
- A hospital-led customer acquisition engine no competitor has: long-standing partnerships with 13,500+ hospitals and maternity clinics across India, through which over 2.4 Million FirstCry-branded baby boxes were distributed during FY 2025-26.
- Full-stack operating model with end-to-end control across sourcing, manufacturing and fulfilment, resting on 800+ contract manufacturing partners across India and overseas plus in-house diaper manufacturing through Swara Baby, Swara Hygiene and Solis Hygiene.
- Proprietary last-mile logistics: RocketBees expanded from 4 to 62 cities during FY 2025-26, delivering approximately 20% faster turnaround times than third-party logistics providers while handling over 40% of online shipment volumes, with FirstCry Qwik delivering in under three hours by turning stores into local fulfilment hubs.
- Omnichannel cross-pollination as a durable moat: 36% of India GMV across the top 50 cities came from customers shopping across both online and offline channels, and such customers show structurally higher basket values, purchase frequency and loyalty.
- A warehouse and delivery network supporting same-day delivery across 25+ cities and next-day delivery across 980+ cities, backed by 84 warehouses and stockists as at March 31, 2026.
- Long customer lifecycle in the parenting category: as children's needs evolve from infancy to adolescence, families keep buying across categories, holding retention high and lifting transaction value year after year.
- A content, community and technology layer that extends the relationship past the point of sale: one of India's largest in-house influencer programmes in the MBK category, a large engaged parenting community, AI tools including Parenting GPT, and 193 Million FirstCry app downloads.
- Category resilience: approximately 85% of GMV comes from non-diapering products, insulating the business from the diapering discounting cycle, and childcare spending is predominantly non-discretionary.
- Market leadership in the GCC: FirstCry is the largest specialist online retailer for MBK products in the UAE by GMV and the leading online-first specialist platform in KSA.
- A proprietary Product Lifecycle Management platform supporting faster innovation, stronger quality assurance and efficient management of home brands.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.
